paraphrase: Having built a house on the hill, why fear the beasts? Having built a house on the seashore, why fear the waves? Having built a house in the market, why be ashamed of noise? Born into the world, when praise and blame come one must not get angry but stay calm, Cennamallikārjuna.
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D.

paraphrase: If hungry, there is alms-food in the villages; if thirsty, tanks, streams and wells; for sleep, the ruined temples; and for the soul's company I have you, Cennamallikārjuna.
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi

paraphrase: I love the Beautiful One who has no death, no decay and no form, no place, no end, no birth; I love him, mother; Cennamallikārjuna is my husband — take these husbands who die and decay and feed them to your kitchen fires.
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi

paraphrase: Like the silkworm that builds its house out of its own love and dies wound round and round in its own threads, I burn with the desires of my heart; Lord, cut through my heart's greed and show me the way out, Cennamallikārjuna.
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi

paraphrase: You can take away the money in the hand, but can you take away the body's glory? You can strip off every cloth one wears, but can you strip the Nothing that covers and veils? For one who wears the light of Cennamallikārjuna, what need is there of cover and jewel?
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi
